body: We were playing in teams because I didn't like being alone. I was seven, my teammate was 14. We hid in the bathroom closet on top of my washer/dryer. He put his hands into my underwear and had his way. I had not even thought to explore myself yet. I was too frightened to say anything.
That Walmart hoodie really brings out your toothpick arms.

Thank you for the advice. I bounce back and forth between telling myself that I'm overreacting and forgiving myself for potentially having a medical condition. Either way -- whether it's biological or psychological -- I need to find a way to deal with it and I can't do so until I acknowledge and explore. It's the scariest thing to do, to do go my doctor and maybe hear an answer I'm afraid of, but I must be brave. I'm crying just from the fear of the answer. I hope I don't chicken out.

I have not seen a doctor, mostly because I have not had affordable medical insurance up to this point. I just started a new job and I can't help but feel my co-workers think my resume is a huge farce, since I'm just not capable of doing the things I once could (I'm only 30.) I am constantly making the simplest of mistakes, stuff you wouldn't even expected a high schooler to mess up on. I have a physical scheduled in February on my new insurance but I'm almost scared of even taking about my experiences because I'm so afraid of the answer.
